title: Local conventions/traps in pkg/storage/unified
answers: Why does GuaranteedUpdate not enforce resource-version optimistic concurrency like typical k8s stores?
What error type do unified storage RPCs return?
Why can a valid-looking resource name be rejected?
Is sql/backend.go the right place to add new storage backend logic?
body: sql/backend.go is legacy and being retired; new backend work belongs in resource/kv.go, not sql/backend.go. Resource versions are derived from Snowflake IDs (sql/backend.go:toMicrosecondRV, around line 851), not simple counters. Optimistic concurrency is enforced via RowsAffected() in checkConflict (backend.go around line 1088), not a read-back comparison. apistore.Storage.GuaranteedUpdate does NOT set the RV precondition by default (apistore/store.go around line 725); do not assume standard k8s RV-based optimistic concurrency always applies here. Server RPC errors are *resourcepb.ErrorResult (HTTP-status-coded, built via resource/errors.go helpers), a separate error model from plain Go error sentinels; mixing them up is a common mistake. Resource keys are strictly validated in resource/keys.go:verifyRequestKeyNamespaceGroupResource; names failing validation.IsValidGrafanaName are rejected at the storage layer. StorageOptions.GVK must be set explicitly per API version (apistore/store.go lines 75-85), not derived; one Go type can back multiple versions.
applies: Applies to code implementing or calling storage.Interface / StorageBackend under pkg/storage/unified; not relevant to legacy sqlstore code outside this package.
